chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Safwan ibn Yahya from Sa'id ibn Yasar from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"Whoever dies and has not performed the Hajj of Islam, and left nothing except the amount equivalent to the expenses of Hajj, then his heirs have more right to what he left; if they wish, they may perform Hajj on his behalf, and if they wish, they may consume it."

Because the first report applies to one upon whom the Hajj of Islam became obligatory, but he did not perform it until his wealth was exhausted, and he died leaving only a small amount, so it became obligatory to perform Hajj on his behalf from some of that amount. And the second report applies to one upon whom Hajj was not obligatory due to lack of means, and he died leaving an amount sufficient for Hajj expenses, so it was not obligatory to perform Hajj on his behalf, because one with this description is not obligated to perform the Hajj of Islam, and his wealth becomes inheritance, and the matter is left to his heirs; if they wish, they perform Hajj on his behalf, and if they wish, they do not. And whoever vows to perform Hajj for Allah, while the Hajj of Islam was already obligatory upon him, then when he dies, the Hajj of Islam is performed on his behalf from the principal of his wealth, and what he vowed is performed on his behalf from one-third of his wealth, if his wealth reaches that amount; otherwise, his guardian should perform the vow Hajj on his behalf as a voluntary act.

key_terms.الْمَوَاقِيتُ: Stations/limits (referring to the portion of wealth)
key_terms.حَجَّةُ الْإِسْلَامِ: The first obligatory Hajj performed by an individual

ai.seo_question: What do heirs do with the money of a deceased person who died without performing Hajj but left enough for its cost?
ai.summary: This narration from Sahih al-Tusi elucidates the juristic distinction between the obligatory Hajj (Hajj al-Islam) and voluntary acts for the deceased, emphasizing that heirs hold discretionary authority over the estate when the deceased left only Hajj-equivalent funds. It further clarifies the procedural handling of specific vows (nadhr) relative to the primary obligation, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the precise conditions of financial capacity (istita'ah) for Hajj liability.
